writeup: TIC 314239566 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.5726 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 2.06 percent, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The transit signal achieves a detection significance of 148.4 in the Box Least Squares periodogram, and pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 38.7, though the centroid offset of 3.9 arcseconds from the target warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unknown object. The machine learning screening score of 0.50 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine astrophysical source rather than an instrumental artifact. All automated data quality checks passed without flagging concerns.
